Profile Chromium trioxide and other chromium compounds are used in industry. Solutions of chromium trioxide are corrosive, acting by oxidation. Repeated contact with chromium and its salts may cause eczematous dermatitis, particularly in hypersensitive per- sons and can also cause deep perforating ulcers known as ‘chrome holes’. If inhaled, chromic dusts cause rhinitis and pain- less ulcers which may perforate the nasal septum; inhalation may cause severe lung damage and inflammation of the eyes. There may also be involvement of the CNS and there is an increased risk of lung cancer. Hexavalent chromium compounds are more dangerous than di- or trivalent compounds. Acute symptoms of poisoning from the ingestion of chromium salts include intense thirst, dizziness, abdominal pain with vom- iting and diarrhoea, hepatic injury, anuria or oliguria, and periph- eral vascular collapse. Kidney damage may lead to fatal uraemia. Treatment is symptomatic and supportive. Protective measures should be taken when handling or working with chromium and its salts. Chromium trioxide was formerly used as a caustic and astrin- gent. Chromium is an essential trace element as described on p.1934. Adverse effects.
